target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:72:    ## ChainDAG validates, stores and serves chain history of valid blocks
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:73:    ## according to the beacon chain state transition. From genesis to the
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:74:    ## finalization point, block history is linear - from there, it branches out
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:75:    ## into a dag with several heads, one of which is considered canonical.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:76:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:77:    ## As new blocks are added, new segments of the chain may finalize,
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:78:    ## discarding now unviable candidate histories.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:79:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:80:    ## In addition to storing blocks, the chaindag also is responsible for
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:81:    ## storing intermediate states in the database that are used to recreate
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:82:    ## chain history at any point in time through a rewinding process that loads
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:83:    ## a snapshots and applies blocks until the desired point in history is
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:84:    ## reached.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:85:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:86:    ## Several indices are kept in memory and database to enable fast lookups -
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:87:    ## their shape and contents somewhat depend on how the chain was
target_workspace/beacon_chain/consensus_object_pools/block_pools_types.nim:88:    ## instantiated: sync from genesis or checkpoint, and therefore, what

target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:40:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:41:    ## Message routing does 3 things:
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:42:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:43:    ## * perform a "quick" sanity check of the message similar to gossip
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:44:    ##   processing - regardless where the message comes from, this check is
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:45:    ##   done so as to protect the internal state of the beacon node
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:46:    ## * broadcast the message to the network - in general, the aim is to start
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:47:    ##   the broadcasting as soon as possible without risking that the node
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:48:    ##   gets descored
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:49:    ## * update the internal state of the beacon node with the data in the
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:50:    ##   message - for example add a block to the dag or an attestation to the
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:51:    ##   attestation pool and fork choice - as a consequence, the message will
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:52:    ##   also be published to event subscribers
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:53:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:54:    ## Because the message router produces messages that will be gossiped, we
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:55:    ## run the messages through the same validation as incoming gossip messages.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:56:    ##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/validators/message_router.nim:57:    ## In most cases, processing of valid messages is identical to that done

target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:33:##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:34:## All JSON responses return the requested data under a data key in the top
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:35:## level of their response.  Additional metadata may or may not be present
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:36:## in other keys at the top level of the response, dependent on the endpoint.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:37:## The rules that require an increase in version number are as follows:

target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:44:##
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:45:## Note that it is possible for a field to be added to an endpoint's data or
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:46:## metadata without an increase in the version number.
target_workspace/beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim:47:##
